title: Production skill routing and visible export approval context
scenarios: Evaluate the unchanged bundled routing corpus with the production eligibility, invocation, and ranking implementation
Prefer a complete requested skill name, reject negated invocations, and retain relevance when confidence scores saturate
Keep explicit-only, human-only, and disabled skills behind their existing invocation policies
Render outgoing file, action, and destination in both the main dialog and the browser approval card
Keep recent untrusted source context separate from the actual outgoing file
Exclude URL credentials and query values, escape labels, and handle missing or malformed legacy context
Deny controlled approvals through the real Electron renderer, preload, IPC, and approval store
Reject nested applicability and explanatory descriptions as explicit CLI invocation while preserving direct conditional commands and later independent requests
Check every original routing expectation, transferring proven human-only, guideline, and descriptive examples to explicit policy contracts; fail policy drift independently of ranking thresholds
Route the retired changelog case through the real installed technical-writing pack without exposing uninstalled pack skills to the base catalogue
notes: Specification plus executable coverage, not an executed eval itself. Run npm run skills:eval-routing -- --strict, the listed unit tests, and qa:routing-export-risk:smoke. The live smoke uses a synthetic isolated profile and real approval persistence, without a provider call or external send. All original prompts remain covered; explicit reviewed contracts replace proven stale expectations and fail if policy or corpus coverage drifts. Ranking and policy results are reported separately; thresholds remain unchanged.
